paper: Gilens & Page 2014, Testing Theories of American Politics, Perspectives on Politics 12(3):564-581, DOI 10.1017/S1537592714001595
fulltext: HELD: PSE mirror PDF 531K/18pp, pdftotext 1074 lines; Model-4 std coef + near-zero nonsignificant + Fig1 0.3/0.18/0.45 verified verbatim in body text.
design: 1,779 policy issues 1981-2002, single multivariate model testing 4 traditions
finding: Economic elites + business interest groups substantial independent impacts; average citizens + mass groups little/no independent influence. Supports Economic-Elite Domination + Biased Pluralism; not Majoritarian Electoral Democracy/Pluralism.
paper_map: Average-citizen preference -> policy ~= 0 independent effect = standing gate g4->0 for the many; business-group capture = priority manipulation at the sovereign layer. Upgrades sovereign section from analogical illustrations to measured political-science mechanism.

numbers.citizens_effect: non-significant near-zero, Majoritarian Electoral Democracy decisively rejected
